title: Sheaf of modules from an indexed basis
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space, $I$ a small type, and $U_i$ opens whose range is a basis. Let $c(i,j)$ satisfy $U_{c(i,j)}=U_i\cap U_j$. Assume every indexed basis cover of $U_i$ has a finite basis refinement. Let $R$ be a sheaf of rings and $Q_i$ an $R(U_i)$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with additive restrictions for every inclusion, satisfying identity, composition and semilinearity. Assume unique gluing for finite covers, with overlap comparisons on $c(i,j)$, including empty covers. Then there is a sheaf $E$ of $R$-modules with linear isomorphisms $E(U_i)\cong Q_i$ commuting with restriction. Every compatible linear family $Q_i\to G(U_i)$ for a sheaf $G$ extends uniquely to $E\to G$; this morphism is an isomorphism if all the family maps are bijective. Distinct indices may represent the same open.

source.place: Section 009H, Tags 009L, 009N, 009T and 009U; choose one index per basis open

proof.text: Set B = range U and choose c(V) with U(c(V)) = V. Define F(V) by restricting scalars on Q(c(V)) along the equality-induced ring map R(V) → R(U(c(V))). Its carrier is Q(c(V)), so the original additive restrictions define rb. Identity and composition follow from rid and rcomp; semilinearity follows from rsmul and functoriality of R.

2. For any i,j with U i=U j, restriction in each direction is inverse to the other:
   apply composition and then identity. These inverse maps identify all representatives.
   In particular the chosen representative of an intersection identifies with cap i j.

Descend finite refinement by indexing C ⊆ B by its subtype, applying hrefine to its chosen representatives, and taking the resulting opens as elements of B. For finite gluing, restrict each overlap equality from the chosen representative of the intersection to cap(c(V_j),c(V_k)). Composition turns it into precisely the overlap hypothesis of hglue. Apply hglue to the chosen indices; the carriers of F are unchanged, so the unique section and its restriction formulas give finite unique gluing on B.

4. Apply exists_sheafOfModules_from_basis. For each original i compose its chosen-basis
   section equivalence with the inverse representative identification of step 2 to obtain
   iota i. Composition proves its restriction law.

Compose each compatible family psi with iota to get linear maps E(U_i) → G(U_i). Apply Mathlib TopCat.Sheaf.restrictHomEquivHom on the indexed basis to the underlying additive maps. The extension is linear: restrict its scalar-linearity equation to a basis neighbourhood of each point, use naturality and the given basis linearity, then sheaf section_ext. Hom uniqueness follows from TopCat.Sheaf.hom_ext. If every psi_i is bijective, each component is bijective because iota_i is a linear equivalence. TopCat.Sheaf.isIso_iff_isIso_basis and reflection of isomorphisms by SheafOfModules.toSheaf give IsIso. No nonempty-index or nonempty-cover assumption is used.

proof_origin.note: Implemented representative descent using restriction of scalars. Existence uses the stated set-basis theorem; the universal property uses the existing Mathlib basis morphism leaf directly.

mathlib_searches.results: Structure-sheaf and chart isomorphisms only; basis topology lemmas only. No matching module gluing or indexed extension declaration.

Existing exists_sheafOfModules_from_basis takes a set of opens, not an indexed basis. Existing gradedModuleAwayRestriction supplies localization comparisons, not finite chart gluing or quasi-coherence of a given sheaf.
